messages:
incbot: PagerDuty alert (PD-8672) -> SEV2: auth-edge clusters reporting sudden spike in 401/403 and some 5xx. Regions: us-west-2, eu-central-1. Probable vector: repeated bearer token probes. Links: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/PD-8672 :rotating_light:

oncall-alex: acked. I’m oncall — paging SRE and Security. @sre-maya @security-ella please join.

sre-maya: on it. pulling logs now. which ingress/app? auth-edge is the gateway layer right? running quick query for 401s grouped by source IP and user-agent.

observability-ron: dashboard shows 401 spike starting 2024-11-12T15:02Z, peak ~15:05Z. top user-agents: `curl/7.68.0`, `python-requests/2.28` and some weird UA `okhttp/3.12.1`. Top source CIDRs: 45.77.12.0/24, 198.51.100.0/25, and multiple from AS6167.

sre-maya: query used (ELK):
```
GET /_search
{ "query": { "bool": { "must": [ {"match": {"http.status_code": 401}}, {"range": {"@timestamp": {"gte":"now-15m"}}} ] } },
"aggs": { "by_ip": { "terms": { "field": "client.ip" , "size": 10}}}
}
```

security-ella: thanks. also grep for "Authorization: Bearer" in debug logs — we need to determine if any tokens leaked into logs or were exfiltrated. shell snippet: 
```
zgrep -i "Authorization: Bearer" /var/log/auth-edge/*.log | head
```

eng-frontend-jared: noticed in sentry some 502s for a small subset of customers, looks correlated with the auth spike. Likely clients are retrying and triggering upstream errors.

ops-priyanka: recommend temporary WAF block on those CIDRs + rate-limit on /auth/token and /auth/refresh. I can push a rule to the edge. Will prepare change.

oncall-alex: do the block. post the change-id here. also we should rotate any short-lived signing keys if they were used with these endpoints. @security-ella please advise which secrets to rotate.

security-ella: prioritize `svc-auth-signer` and `token-proxy` service tokens. We need an inventory of tokens used in the edge clusters. If logs show bearer tokens present, escalate to SEV1. For now: 1) snapshot current logs (immutable) 2) block offending CIDRs 3) rotate tokens 4) scrub logs that contain secrets and preserve copies in a secured bucket.

deploy-bot: Run started: `edge/waf/2024-11-12/block-cidrs-45-198` by ops-priyanka. Status: in_progress.

ops-priyanka: applied WAF rules: block 45.77.12.0/24 and 198.51.100.0/25, rate-limit 10r/s on /auth/* for anonymous UAs. Change-id: ch-20241112-71. Rolling out to us-west-2 and eu-central-1 now.

deploy-bot: Run completed: ch-20241112-71 -> success.

sre-maya: after block, 401 spike dropped ~85% in 3m. tail shows residual probes from new IPs, likely rotating botnets. Need long-term mitigations: WAF rule tuning + per-tenant throttling.

eng-frontend-jared: hotfix ready to turn off verbose debug logging for auth-edge (no more dumping headers). Will push a config toggle now. commit: 5f1b2c8.

eng-frontend-jared: pushed config: `AUTH_EDGE_DEBUG=false` and restarted auth-edge pods in canary. Rolling to remaining nodes if metrics look good.

security-ella: running token-scan on snapped logs to detect patterns of `Bearer [A-Za-z0-9\\-_.]+`. If we find full tokens present in logs, we rotate immediately and notify customers as required by policy.

security-ella: scan result: 3 matches in eu-central-1 debug logs, appears to be truncated tokens (last 4 chars visible) but still treat as possible exposure. Recommend rotating `svc-auth-signer` and rotating any session tokens with TTL < 24h.

oncall-alex: approved rotation. @ops-priyanka coordinate with platform to rotate `svc-auth-signer` and update deployments. Use secret manager staged rotation and fallback.

ops-priyanka: running staged rotation: step1 create new key in Secrets Manager, step2 add new key to canary pods, step3 promote, step4 revoke old key. Commands: 
```
aws secretsmanager create-secret --name svc-auth-signer-rot-20241112 --secret-string file://newkey.json
kubectl set env deployment/auth-edge AUTH_SIGNER_SECRET=svc-auth-signer-rot-20241112 -n platform
```

deploy-bot: Rotation job started: rotate-svc-auth-signer-20241112. Status: in_progress.

deploy-bot: Rotation job completed successfully. New secret staged to canary, promoted to all clusters. Old secret disabled.

security-ella: old secret disabled and scheduled for purge in 7 days. Created ticket SEC-4921 to track post-incident forensic export and customer notification draft.

legal-sam: loop me in when we confirm tokens leaked. need list of affected customers and window of exposure.

observability-ron: quick impact numbers: ~0.4% of total auth traffic returned 401 during spike window. Roughly ~1,200 distinct client IPs hit endpoints with elevated failure. Customer-facing errors concentrated in 6 tenants (IDs: t-102, t-214, t-330, t-405, t-601, t-904).

security-ella: triage decision: treat as SEV2 for now since WAF and rotation mitigated primary vectors. If any evidence of exfiltration or token reuse appears, escalate to SEV1. Create postmortem runbook and assign owners.

oncall-alex: handoff: SRE (maya) + Security (ella) will own post-incident follow-up. Ops-priyanka continues with secrets lifecycle cleanup. Legal (sam) to prepare customer comms if needed. I’ll follow up in 2 hours for status and hand off next oncall. :white_check_mark: 

security-ella: creating secure archive of snapped logs and moving to s3://redwood-secure/incident-archives/PD-8672 with restricted ACLs. Also running additional scans for outbound traffic anomalies.

sre-maya: opening postmortem ticket PM-6784 with timeline, mitigation steps, and action items (WAF tuning, remove debug logging, secrets rotation automation). Assigning to eng-frontend, ops, security.

oncall-alex: thanks everyone. monitoring until handoff. if anything new appears, re-ping this thread.

incbot: Incident update logged: PD-8672 -> state: mitigated (SEV2). Handoff to followup.
